content.overview: Section 105 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 defines a lease of immovable property as a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value, to be rendered periodically or on specified occasions to the transferor by the transferee, who accepts the transfer on such terms. The transferor is the lessor; the transferee is the lessee; the price is called the premium and the money, share, service or other thing to be so rendered is called the rent.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Right to enjoy immovable property? (2) Certain time or perpetuity? (3) Consideration — premium and/or rent? (4) Lessor and lessee?
content.study:
Lease transfers a limited right to enjoy, not full ownership (contrast sale). Duration may be fixed or perpetual. Consideration may be premium, rent, or both.

How leases are made is governed by s. 107.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Definition
sections.body: Transfer of a right to enjoy immovable property for a certain time or in perpetuity, for premium and/or rent.

sections.heading: Consideration
sections.body: Premium (price) and/or rent (periodical or on specified occasions).

sections.heading: Duration
sections.body: Certain time (express or implied) or perpetuity.

sections.heading: Link to s. 107
sections.body: How leases are made — registered instrument / delivery of possession rules under s. 107.

examples.title: Yearly lease
examples.body: Owner transfers right to enjoy a shop for one year for monthly rent — lease under s. 105; formality under s. 107.

hypotheticals.question: Does a lease transfer ownership like a sale?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. A lease transfers only a right to enjoy for the term; ownership remains with the lessor.

distinctions.title: Lease (s. 105) vs sale (s. 54)
distinctions.left: Right to enjoy for a term or perpetuity; rent/premium.

misconceptions.trap: Every licence to occupy is a lease under s. 105.
misconceptions.correction: Lease requires transfer of a right to enjoy on the statutory terms; licences and pure permissions are distinct.
